title: Physical-World Data Guides by Industry and Use Case
heading: Physical-world data by use case
description: Find source-backed guides for property, lending, insurance, power, logistics, retail, and public projects. Start with the decision you need to make.

checklistTitle: Start with the record your decision needs

checks.title: Identify the site or asset
checks.detail: Use the correct parcel, building, facility, or utility connection. Record the boundary or ID you are making a decision about.

checks.title: Check the date and scope
checks.detail: Read the source, effective date, and fields that matter. Keep planned, approved, and operating assets distinct.

checks.title: Test it on real work
checks.detail: Use a guide’s named case or downloadable sample, then repeat the check on a site or portfolio you know.

guides.label: Match the correct parcel and property unit

guides.label: Trace who owns a commercial property
guides.detail: Follow a deed, an entity filing, and the property link without assuming a shared name proves common ownership.

guides.label: Match building footprints to parcels
guides.detail: Compare mapped structures and their identifiers before aggregating a site or underwriting a portfolio.

guides.label: Check hospital, school, and fire service coverage
guides.detail: Compare travel times, grade-specific attendance maps, and emergency service boundaries for a proposed housing development.

guides.label: Compare housing vacancy and rent burden by census tract
guides.detail: Match tract boundaries across Census releases and test whether changes in vacancy and rent burden exceed sampling uncertainty.

guides.label: Find and verify building permits
guides.detail: Check permit status, work scope, and the issuing agency record at the property level.

guides.label: Look up building energy use by address
guides.detail: Compare annual energy, reporting property IDs, meter scope and floor area before estimating operating costs or screening a retrofit.

guides.label: Check open building violations and correction records
guides.detail: Use the original building ID to verify summons status, balance and proof of correction on separate records.

guides.label: Screen land for wetlands and hydric soils

title: U.S. site selection due diligence checklist
heading: Site selection due diligence
description: Use the tract, project requirements and dated evidence to decide whether a site belongs on your shortlist. Find field-tested guides for industrial, retail and energy projects.

checklistTitle: What to verify before making the shortlist

checks.title: The tract and the use
checks.detail: Get the current offering boundary and parcel IDs. Sketch the building, yard and access inside the usable area. Check permitted use, flood, wetlands and other land constraints against that layout.

checks.title: The service the project needs
checks.detail: Write down the required MW, water, wastewater and access by phase and date. Use local records to find who serves the tract, then ask each provider what can be delivered and which work it depends on.

checks.title: Evidence for each decision
checks.detail: Save the dated source and the tract or facility it describes. Give every open item an owner and a deadline. Keep a broker estimate, a screening result and a signed commitment distinct in the shortlist.

worksheet.label: Download the site evidence worksheet
worksheet.detail: Use one row for each requirement, tract and delivery phase.

title: Commercial property underwriting guides
heading: Commercial property underwriting
description: Build the property file before you quote. Match the building, verify flood, wildfire and hail evidence, and test the data behind the submission.
imageAlt: Illustration of a commercial building at the edge of dry Southern California hills
checklistTitle: What belongs in the property file?

checks.title: The building on the submission
checks.detail: Match the address, footprint and building ID to the statement of values, the schedule of insured locations and amounts. Review shared addresses and older footprints before applying a hazard result.

checks.title: Evidence dated to the decision
checks.detail: Keep the publisher, vintage and original result for each hazard layer or event. Record what was in effect on the quote or renewal date and when you retrieved it.

checks.title: The evidence still needed
checks.detail: Keep uncertain matches and coverage gaps visible. Request a dated inspection, roof scope or loss history when the available records leave a building-level question open.

title: How to Evaluate Physical-World Data APIs
heading: Evaluating physical-world data APIs
description: Run eight real tests against physical-world data APIs. Compare parcel identity, zoning, flood exposure, property changes, underwriting records, power dates and charging.
imageAlt: Aerial view of Midtown Manhattan with the Digital Tax Map base lot for 432 Park Avenue outlined in gold.
imageCaption: 432 Park Avenue. The outline shows the Digital Tax Map base lot. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS, 2024.
checklistTitle: How to run a vendor trial

checks.title: Freeze the inputs and date
checks.detail: Write down the decision, exact location or ID, geometry, requested fields and date. Give every provider the same inputs. Alongside known answers, include a record that moved, split or should come back unknown.

checks.title: Set acceptance criteria before the demo
checks.detail: Use the worksheet’s dated reference result. Confirm the endpoint and what its fields measure. Record the returned entity, geometry, units, source and effective date. Keep an unavailable field separate from a failed request.

checks.title: Run it at production volume
checks.detail: Repeat the test across your actual counties and workload. Measure response times, failed requests and cost per usable result. Check retention, redistribution and audit rights for the data you will store or show, then document the gap owner and release decision.

worksheet.label: Download the vendor evaluation worksheet
worksheet.detail: Eight exact test inputs with dated reference results, original source links and space to record your vendor’s response.

guides.label: Match the right parcel and condo unit
guides.detail: At 432 Park Avenue, compare base lot 1012920033, billing lot 1012927502 and unit 1012921303. Ask which record supplies the geometry.

guides.label: Replay a parcel split with a retained ID
guides.detail: Compare BBL 3039470001 before and after the November 20, 2026 split. The retained lot kept its ID and lost roughly 21,169 square feet.

guides.detail: At Brooklyn Army Terminal, the published point is in Zone AE. The parcel overlay puts 19.9% of the lot in that zone.

guides.detail: For 25 Water Street, compare 1,323 total units in MapPLUTO with 1,320 dwelling units on the initial occupancy issuance.

guides.detail: For Rosemead project 31031, compare what a June 30 quote could establish with what the July 8 council packet later documented.

guides.detail: Compare the required and projected dates for PJM b4068.2 with the separate customer service estimate in AEP Ohio’s study.

guides.detail: AFDC stations 322368 and 388708 list 16 DC fast ports combined. Ask for the separate observation that establishes live status.
